why: Mountain Project describes the whole line as a winter snow and ice couloir, snowfield and cornice finish on a Cabinets face, with no glacier.
The American Alpine Journal account describes a 16-pitch summer rock route from Granite Lake with scrambling and no ice or glacier.
The first-ascent report describes a March ice and neve couloir on the northeast buttress of A Peak ending in a walk-off, with no glacier.
The Mountain Project area page gives only grades and permit notes, nothing about the face's approach or ice.
Two searches found no page naming this route; other South Tower lines were described but not this one.
The AAJ article places the face above old glacier moraine but does not say where Stella starts or whether it touches the glacier.
Mountain Project describes a snow and ice couloir with no glacier mentioned, but not how the party reaches its base, so a glacier on the way in is not ruled out.
Mountain Project describes a short snow gully inside Crook Cirque needing deep snow, but gives no approach and does not address the glacier remnant.
Mountain Project describes a west-side ridge reached from the PCT straight to the summit pinnacle, and lists the glacier routes separately.
Mountain Project describes the approach from Timberline and four pitches on the rock toe of Illumination Rock with no glacier crossing.
Mountain Project has the party step onto the Milk Creek Glacier on 30 to 40 degree snow and says no active crevasses are apparent, a single account that does not settle it.
The trip reports found were blocked or described only the ice pillar start, not the approach.
A search found no page describing this route.
Mountain Project describes a snow and debris ramp into an ice couloir with no glacier mentioned, while club listings ask for glacier gear, so the approach is not settled.
Mountain Project describes moderate snow into a gully to the Wy'east ridge with no glacier mentioned, but gives no approach.
Mountain Project describes a snow gully and ridge to the summit past a fumarole with no glacier mentioned, but nothing on the lower approach.
Mountain Project says only to approach via Devil's Kitchen and describes gullies up the rime-covered Steel Cliff, without covering the approach.
Only a search snippet described the route as a Class 3 to 4 gully climb from Wing Lake; no page that could be read confirmed it or the snow.
